title: Chapter 190: Don't be Scared, I'm a Visitor
html:
The corridor fell so silent that not even breathing could be heard. Unaware of what Chen Ge had done, the “ghost” inside the box waited for the perfect moment to deliver his fatal scare.

Hidden in the corner, Chen Ge silently counted down. After thirty seconds, something creaked inside the box. The actor had probably grown tired of holding the same position.

By comparison, Chen Ge resembled a seasoned hunter. He hunched forward and crept closer. At forty seconds, the “ghost” began to wonder why his visitor had not appeared and shifted position, trying to improve his view.

The silent standoff approached its climax. With three seconds remaining, Chen Ge stepped in front of the box and blocked its door. At that instant, a woman’s shriek erupted inside. Unlike Black Friday, Wedding Dress opened at full volume.

Already tense from searching for Chen Ge, the actor heard the shrill scream directly behind him. He slammed into the door and, in his panic, tripped over the prop meant to frighten his victim. He crashed to the bottom of the box.

“What was that sound? What was that sound!”

The cramped darkness became his worst nightmare. The female ghost sounded close enough to touch. He pounded frantically on the door, while Chen Ge, having anticipated everything, helpfully stepped back against it to keep it shut.

“What is that? Let me out!” Concerned that holding the door might waste too much energy, Chen Ge soon moved aside.

The door burst open, and a male “ghost” in a patient’s gown crawled out, his face covered in fake blood. Clutching his chest, he gulped air before collapsing in the corridor like a traumatized survivor.

“Don’t be afraid. I’m only a visitor.” Chen Ge spoke naturally into the recorder, then retrieved his phone and silenced the alarm as though nothing unusual had happened.

Cold sweat mingled with the fake blood on the actor’s face. He looked at Chen Ge with indescribable emotion and appeared utterly pitiful.

“Why did you fall? Are you injured?” Chen Ge peered inside the box. Two custom mannequin heads lay on the floor, one stripped of its long wig. “You planned to scare me with something this horrible? How wicked.”

Chen Ge planned to go help the man, but the man crawled away from him. “Don’t touch me! Go ahead… I can stand up on my own.”

“You sure? You look so pale.”

“That’s the makeup! Leave me alone and keep moving!” The actor struggled back into the box and shut the door.

“Be careful, then.” Chen Ge reset the alarm. Wedding Dress was certainly useful. Something struck the back of his head. He turned to find the “female corpse” still swinging overhead.

He reached out to grab the body’s feet. They felt cold to his touch. There was even a name written on the body’s patient outfit—Xu Zhenzhen.

“The handiwork is not bad but still worse than the mannequins inside my Haunted House.”

Having delivered his critique, Chen Ge continued. As he turned the corner, the “corpse” behind him began to sway again.

He had now entered Tian Teng Medical School proper. Messages in dried blood covered the white walls: “I don’t want to die” and “Give me back my organs.”

“This Haunted House’s background sure is complicated. I suppose the aim is for the visitor to explore the place on their own and come up with the solution to reconstruct the actual origin story.”

Painted windows lined the corridor. Combined with carefully timed lighting, they created the illusion of something racing past outside. The designer was unquestionably skilled. Some windows were solid, while others concealed openings. As Chen Ge passed the fourth, a hand shot out and grabbed him. At the same moment, the ceiling clicked, releasing a hidden mannequin head that rolled down into his arms.

Anyone else might have screamed. Chen Ge had never felt calmer. He raised the head with a nostalgic expression. “When I was four or five, I used to run around carrying fake heads just like this. How time flies.”

The actor gripping him from beyond the window went still.He ran around with fake heads when he was four or five? What kind of childhood did he have?

The actor silently released him and withdrew behind the window. The lighting gradually dimmed, leaving green lamps spaced every few yards. The corridor narrowed, and operating rooms began appearing on either side.

“Operating rooms already?” Chen Ge stopped outside the first and surveyed his surroundings. Countless Trial Missions had taught him to confirm a room was safe before entering.

Glancing back, he spotted the security guard, still wearing his ghost mask, helping the earlier actor out of the box.

“Normally, there should be a ghost chasing after the visitors, and that would increase the excitement of the experience.”

The actor’s limbs had gone limp, leaving him unable to stand. The guard struggled awkwardly to support him, destroying the frightening atmosphere.

“Two of them are accounted for, so why do I feel a third person following me?” Chen Ge filed the question away and entered the autopsy room. Tables had been pushed against the walls, and fake blood covered the mannequins, creating a grisly scene.

“Japanese and Western attractions certainly love this style.” Chen Ge sought dread and terror; gore merely expressed violence. He scanned the room and, to his surprise, found no hidden actor—only damaged mannequins.

Examining several, he discovered that each lacked a different organ. More intriguingly, every mannequin wore a patient’s gown bearing the same name: Xu Zhenzhen.

“Is this a special request by the boss?” Chen Ge tried to go over the video he had seen in the security stop in his mind. There was no mention of this name.

“Xu Zhenzhen? Could she be the woman who was featured inside the video?”

Chen Ge exited the autopsy room. The security guard and the man inside the box had disappeared; they seemed to have left the Haunted House.
